results.evidence: No outside description found calls the pitch either sparsely or well protected. One route page says the easy-fifth pitches are a good place for a beginner to practise placing gear; a club route page says a rope and basic rock pro help beginners; a trip report found the pitch easy enough to solo. None states that protection is sparse, so the four 'sparse' fields cannot be confirmed and the overview's 'well-protected' cannot be adopted either. Settled by a route description that characterises the gear placements on the chimney.

results.evidence: A club route page states there is one short rock pitch to gain the summit. An independent trip report describes the easiest route as requiring a single pitch of low-angle rock and a single-pitch rappel. The row's own pitch_detail labels only one row P1, and bail/overview describe one pitch.

results.fact: Car-to-car time: timing.totalHrs 3.5 vs itinerary 'roughly 4-6 hours car-to-car'
results.evidence: PUBLISHED TIMES total 3.5 h (sections 1.25+0.75+1.5) while the itinerary prose says roughly 4-6 hours car-to-car. Not researched to two sources in this pass; settled by two outside car-to-car times for Castle alone from Reflection Lakes.

The land manager's trail page gives 7.2 miles round trip and 2,955 ft of gain to the 5,700 ft saddle. An independent hiking-guide page gives 7.2 miles round trip and reaches the pass at 3.6 miles. One-way is therefore 3.6 mi = 5.8 km; the stored 7.3 was the round-trip mileage stored as km.

results.correct_value: The Class 3 gully is the bypass; the Class 4 step is the optional direct variant
results.evidence: beta, rock_grade, pitch_detail[1-2], pro_tips[1], hazards and the baseFinding all say the bypass is the Class 3 gully and the Class 4 rock step is the direct line; the overview alone calls the Class 4 line the bypass. An outside trail description agrees: the summit scramble is Class IV direct, with a slightly longer, less technical Class III alternative via a gully.

results.correct_value: July through September is the usual window
results.evidence: season (Jul-Sep), approach_variants season (Jul-Sep; saddle corniced into June), approach (cornices into June) and climate (spring snow to early June; summer Jul-Sep) agree against best_season's 'June through early October'. An outside hiking guide says the route is best saved for mid to late summer and early fall when snow is absent.

results.evidence: Summit coordinates put Eagle Peak (46.7558, -121.7792) north-west of Chutla Peak (46.7528, -121.7750), and the peak is described as on the north-west/west end of the range, so the baseFinding's 'a quarter mile east along the ridge' from the Eagle-Chutla saddle looks wrong, and one trail description ends the scramble by turning back west (left), matching climbing_route. But the same description says the climbers' path leading right goes to Chutla, contradicting pro_tips[3], while beta and baseFinding send the path east to the rock step; left/right cues cannot be settled by two independent route descriptions, and fixing only the compass word would leave the baseFinding contradicting itself. Settled by a second detailed route description of the saddle-to-summit line.

results.fact: Rope needed for the couloir rappel
results.evidence: The only rappel-length statement found (usually more than 100 ft, double rope recommended, a 70 m rope may suffice in high snow) describes the rappel from the top of Lover's Lane INTO the Zipper, not the Zipper's own descent rappel; it appears to have been copied into this row's descent_text. The Zipper's own route page says a 30 m rope works for running belays but gives no rappel length, and trip reports reachable did not state one. Settled by a source giving the length of the rappel from the Zipper's dead-tree notch.

The route page gives 1000 ft in 3 pitches and says a 30 m rope works for a running belay, so the ~100 m rows are simul-climbing blocks rather than belayed pitches; but each row names a stationary belay anchor, and no source gives pitch lengths or belay spacing. Settled by a pitch-by-pitch source, or an owner decision to relabel the rows as running-belay blocks.
